attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his post. He relies on unnamed sources but states the claim as his own.

semantics.note: In context, 'this' means the OpenAI infrastructure (~$87B of capex). The proposition keeps his sourcing qualifier and says 'Microsoft's operational capacity', as he did. The claim is firm, not hedged.

contract.note: Reading 'vast majority' as well over half is ordinary. Accepting power, GPUs or asset value is generous, and the window up to the post date is reasonable. The 'all compute vs AI-only' ambiguity is flagged, but no evidence measures either one, so it does not change the result.

evidence.note: CFO says new GPUs go first to first-party products and R&D, and Azure customers get the remainder. That covers only new GPUs and gives no OpenAI share, so it is not a measurement of the claim.
OpenAI is ~45% of commercial RPO, which is contracted backlog, not operational capacity. Wrong metric, so context only.

reviews.rationale: The contract needs a disclosure or credible measurement of OpenAI's share of Microsoft's in-service capacity in early-to-mid 2026. Neither item gives one: e1 describes how new GPUs are allocated and e2 is a backlog share. The packet says no such measurement exists. The claim cannot be confirmed or refuted.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: Keeps both the value judgment ('cost too much') and the hedged 'appear to' on linear scaling. Framed as an observation, but its firm parts are evaluative with no benchmark.

contract.note: Fair to treat 'too expensive' as a value judgment with no benchmark, and the linear-scaling remark as hedged and unspecific (no company, cost measure or period). Nothing firm is left to score.

evidence.note: Microsoft says AI investment and usage weighed on gross margin, partly offset by efficiency gains. That is one company's blended margin and does not test linear cost scaling.

reviews.rationale: 'Too expensive' and 'cost too much to run' are value judgments with no benchmark. The linear-scaling part is hedged ('appear') and names no company, metric or period. There is no firm checkable proposition, so this is not adjudicable.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'sometimes' and both money clauses. The quality judgment is subjective and rhetorical. The checkable core is that Anthropic still loses money despite large enterprise payments.

contract.note: Reading 'still lose money' as a company-level reported loss is ordinary, and Q1 2026 as the last full quarter before the post is reasonable. Q2 2026, which contains the post date, shows operating income but still a large net loss, so the contract's contradiction test (profitable on both bases) is not met either way.

evidence.note: S-1 quarterly table: operating loss of about $1.67B for the quarter ended Mar 31, 2026. Filed Oct 26, before the evaluation date.
Same table: net loss of about $14.4B in Q1 2026, mostly from non-cash fair-value charges. Still a reported loss.
S-1 risk factor says a large portion of revenue comes from enterprise customers. That meets the enterprise element of the support condition.

reviews.rationale: Anthropic's S-1 shows an operating and a net loss in Q1 2026, with a large share of revenue from enterprises. That meets the support condition. The quality judgment and the 'subsidized product' clause are not scored. Q2 2026 operating income is noted, but that quarter still had a net loss and it is outside the chosen period.

attribution.note: Zitron's own summary sentence in his post.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'do not appear' hedge and the scope 'outside of OpenAI and Anthropic'. The first clause is hedged. The 'only way' clause is firm but sweeping.

contract.note: The contract admits the first clause is hedged and its evidence is RPO rather than revenue. Reading 'only way' as each lab deal depending on the hyperscaler's own investment is plausible in context, but it is a reading the drafter supplied. The hedged first clause should not decide the score.

evidence.note: Microsoft RPO excluding OpenAI grew 26% YoY to Mar 2026. That cuts against the impression for Microsoft, but it still includes Anthropic, is year over year, and is backlog rather than revenue.
Microsoft RPO excluding OpenAI grew 28% YoY at Dec 2025, but it includes the Anthropic commitment. Covers Microsoft only.

reviews.rationale: The first clause is hedged and is not scored. For the firm 'only way' clause, the packet has nothing linking each lab compute deal to hyperscaler investment, and no backlog or revenue excluding both labs at Alphabet or Amazon. Microsoft's figures still include Anthropic. The evidence does not settle the claim.
